jobs.occupation: Project Engineer – 12-Month Maternity Cover
jobs.description:
Are you ready to take the next step in your engineering career? We are looking for a motivated and ambitious Project Engineer to join our Investment Department at Nordic & Baltic on a 12-month maternity cover.

This is a unique opportunity to gain valuable experience working on high-impact industrial investment projects as part of a professional and collaborative team. During the 12-month period, you will work closely with experienced Project Managers and technical specialists, gaining hands-on experience in project development, technical evaluations, and on-site implementation.

**Your role

**As Project Engineer, you will be part of a team responsible for planning and executing strategic investment projects across our sites. You will support the development and implementation of projects from early-stage feasibility through to execution and handover.

This position is ideal for someone with a mechanical engineering background who is eager to develop their project management skills and gain experience in an industrial environment.

Key responsibilities

• 
Support the planning, budgeting, and execution of industrial investment projects

• 
Participate in feasibility studies, technical evaluations, and risk assessments

• 
Collaborate with internal stakeholders, technical specialists, and external suppliers

• 
Monitor project progress and assist in ensuring delivery on time, within scope, and budget

• 
Contribute to the continuous development of investment project tools and processes

• 
Support operational activities within the Investment Department

• 
Assist Project Managers with coordination and follow-up of project activities

• 
Support implementation and follow-up at project sites when required

What we’re looking for

• 
A degree in mechanical engineering or a related technical field

• 
1–3 years of relevant experience, for example in project engineering, site engineering/management, maintenance, or production

• 
An interest in industrial plants, technical investment projects, and project management

• 
Strong problem-solving skills and a hands-on mindset

• 
Good communication skills in English; Danish is an advantage but not a requirement

• 
A structured and collaborative approach to your work

• 
Willingness to travel occasionally to our project sites if needed

**We offer

**Aalborg Portland is an ambitious and professional workplace with a strong focus on employee development. Through structured development discussions, we continuously support both the professional and personal growth of our employees.

As part of the Investment Department, you will have the opportunity to work alongside experienced colleagues and gain valuable insight into large-scale industrial projects. You will become part of an informal workplace characterized by close collaboration, knowledge sharing, and open dialogue.

We offer an environment with freedom with responsibility and flexibility, where you will have the opportunity to take ownership of your tasks and develop your skills throughout the maternity cover period.

**Employment

**This is a 12-month fixed-term position covering maternity leave, with employment starting as soon as possible.

**How to apply

**If the position sounds interesting, please send your application and CV. Interviews will be held on an ongoing basis, and we therefore encourage you to apply as soon as possible. We reserve the right to close the recruitment process once the right candidate has been found.

**More about us

**Since 2004, Aalborg Portland has been part of the Cementir Group. The Nordic & Baltic Region of the Cementir Group comprises four business units, with Aalborg Portland A/S as the largest and other ready mixed concrete and aggregates businesses under Unicon A/S in Denmark, Unicon AS in Norway, and AB Sydsten in Sweden.

Aalborg Portland is Europe’s largest cement plant, operating seven kiln lines and a unique dock facility with direct access to global logistics. With raw material resources located in immediate proximity and a distribution network of nine terminals across Denmark and Northern Europe, Aalborg Portland serves customers throughout Europe, with its primary market in Scandinavia. Denmark remains the strongest market, where the company holds more than 90% market share. They have around 300 dedicated employees.

Aalborg Portland is also leading the industry’s green transition being ‘Part of the Solution’ !   Under the project name ACCSION, the company plans to build Denmark’s largest CO₂ capture facility, which will make Aalborg Portland CO₂-neutral for its own emissions. ACCSION will capture and store 1.4 million tonnes of CO₂ per year and enable the production of cement types with an ultralow CO₂ footprint.

Aalborg Portland Nordic & Baltic offers equal opportunities for all and have an active focus on fostering a work environment that is free from discrimination and where employees are treated with dignity and respect. PhD position in Compilation Principles for Reversible Languages (MSCA Doctoral Network E-CoRe, DC7), University of Copenhagen
jobs.description:
PhD position in Compilation Principles for Reversible Languages (MSCA Doctoral Network E-CoRe, DC7), University of Copenhagen
 
 The position is doctoral candidate DC7, “Compilation Principles for Reversible Languages", in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network E-CoRe. The position is available from 1 January 2027, or after agreement.
 
 Job description
 The Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section, part of the Department of Computer Science (DIKU), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for a 3-year PhD position on compilation principles for reversible languages.
 
 The project
 The position is funded by the European Union under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks (MSCA-DN) programme, grant agreement no. 101120187. The project advances the science and practice of reversible computing for a sustainable digital future. Energy is a main concern in society: IT accounts for an estimated 10% of global energy consumption. Reversible computation discards no information and therefore avoids the fundamental energy lower bound of conventional computing. The network trains a cohort of doctoral candidates who will improve and popularise reversible languages, algorithms, and architectures for energy-intensive applications. 

  Read more about the network at https://e-core.nws.cs.unibo.it/.
 
 The position is open for talented candidates with a master’s degree, who want to pursue a PhD degree in Computer Science.

  DC7: The successful PhD candidate will work on compilation principles and techniques for reversible languages. The candidate can build on the work by project members. 

  Concretely, the work includes the following:

   	
• Studying techniques for translating high-level reversible languages into efficient low-level reversible and irreversible representations. 	
• Designing optimisation techniques for reversible languages, including foundational methods and novel approaches to program analysis and code generation. 	
• Implementing prototype compilers to evaluate optimisation techniques, alongside a benchmark suite specifically designed for reversible compilation and empirical evaluation. 	
• Publishing the results at international conferences and in peer-reviewed journals.   Planned Secondments: Technische Hochschule Mittelhessen (Germany), University of Manchester (UK).

  Key criteria for the assessment of applicants for the position:  

  The candidate must have a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish Master's degree) in Computer Science or a closely related field, obtained by the recruitment date.

  Certified copy of original Master of Science diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in a language other than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.

  As a prerequisite for a PhD fellowship employment, your master’s degree must be equivalent to a Danish master’s degree. We encourage you to read more in the assessment database: https://ufsn.dk/english/education/recognition-and-transparency/find-assessments/assessment-database/ 

  Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science.

  Other important criteria are:

   	
• Strong academic record and motivation for doctoral research.  	
• Experience in compiler design, program analysis, and language semantics, regardless of programming paradigm, is an advantage. Prior knowledge of reversible computing is not needed. 	
• Ability to work independently, take initiative, and collaborate effectively in an international research environment. Proactive and team-oriented approach to work. 	
• Proficiency in written and spoken English. 	
• Willingness and ability to travel and undertake secondments at other project partners.   The successful candidate will be employed as a PhD student at the Department of Computer Science at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Copenhagen, and will collaborate closely with the group at the University of Southern Denmark, Odense, which is also an E-CoRe partner. The position may involve co-supervising related student projects. The PhD student is expected to participate in the activities of the research section and in the training programme of the E-CoRe network.
 The main supervisor is Professor Robert Glück (e-mail: glueck@di.ku.dk), whose current research focus is on programming languages, reversible computing, program generation, and metaprogramming.

  Start date:    1 January 2027, or after agreement with the cohort of the MSCA-DN

  Duration:      3 years

  The successful candidate will conduct independent research related to the topics above at the Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section, Department of Computer Science (DIKU). We expect the candidate to engage in an active research environment and take part in student guidance.

  Note: Another job opening for DC1 “Reversible Programming Languages” is available. More information: XXX-LINK-TO-DC1.
 
 Mobility rule
 The researcher must not have resided or carried out his/her/their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately before the recruitment date. Short stays as holidays and compulsory military service and/or Refugee Convention 1951 are disregarded.

  Eligibility as Doctoral Candidate (DC)
 The recruited DC must be doctoral candidate, i.e. not already in possession of a doctoral degree on the first day of employment. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree will not be considered eligible.
 
 Workplace description 
 The Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section is part of the Department of Computer Science (DIKU) at the Faculty of Science, located on the North Campus in Copenhagen. At the section we research topics such as algorithmic aspects of programming, compiler technology, functional programming, reversible and quantum computing. You will be part of an international group of PhD students, postdocs, and faculty working at the intersection of programming languages, theory of computing, and various applications.

  More information about PLTC and DIKU can be found at https://di.ku.dk/english/research/pltc/  and https://di.ku.dk/english/.

  Terms of employment 
 Salary, pension and terms of employment will be in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organization. Currently, the monthly salary starts at DKK 31,845 / approx. EUR 4,260 (August 2026-level). 
 Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.
 
 The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  Further information
 For further information, please contact Professor Robert Glück (e-mail: glueck@di.ku.dk).

  International applicants may find this link useful: https://ism.ku.dk/ (International Staff Mobility) or https://www.workindenmark.dk/.

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• Master of Science diploma and transcript of records. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor will do. 	
• Publication list (if any).   Deadline for applications: Sunday 1 November 2026, 23:59 PM CET.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee which will consist of both internal (UCPH) and external members. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed, each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You may read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.
 
 The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: PhD Scholarship in Sustainable Supply Chain Management and Organization - DTU Management
jobs.description:
Are you a collaborative and ambitious master's graduate with strong intercultural awareness and a curiosity for exploring sustainability challenges across different contexts and disciplines? Would you like to help shape the next generation of sustainable and regenerative global supply chains through a unique collaboration between the Technical University of Denmark (DTU) and the University of Nairobi, Kenya? DTU Management (Department of Technology, Management, and Economics) invites applications for a three-year PhD scholarship at the intersection of supply chain management and organization studies. Focusing on global agricultural commodity chains, the project explores how supply chains can create positive environmental and social impacts rather than simply reducing negative ones. It examines regenerative approaches that renew ecological and social systems while being collectively organized with local communities.

The PhD position is anchored at DTU Management and contributes to the department's strategic focus on developing viable and sustainable systems. You will join an international research environment at the forefront of sustainable supply chain management and organization studies, collaborating with researchers and partners in Denmark and Kenya. The project combines literature-based and empirical research on regenerative agri-food supply chains with fieldwork and data collection in Denmark and Kenya. The project will be supervised by Associate Professor Lærke Højgaard Christiansen and Assistant Professor Lara Schilling at DTU and will include an extended research stay at the University of Nairobi under the co-supervision of Senior Lecturer Thomas Ombati and Lecturer Veronica Wambui Mwangi. 

Based in Copenhagen – consistently ranked among the world's most livable cities – you will enjoy a high quality of life, a safe and sustainable urban environment, and a thriving cultural scene. At the same time, you'll be part of a vibrant, interdisciplinary research community at one of Europe's top technical universities, known for its commitment to innovation, societal impact, and diversity.

Responsibilities and qualifications
As a PhD candidate, you will investigate how global agricultural commodity chains, such as tea or coffee, can be managed based on regenerative principles. The project offers a unique opportunity to develop an international and interdisciplinary research profile at the intersection of organization studies and supply chain management. As part of the DTU Management PhD Program, you will follow a structured research and training program that combines independent research, academic coursework, teaching, and professional development.

Mandatory requirements:

• You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.
• An educational background in the social sciences 
• A familiarity with supply chain management, organization studies, or related fields such as (human) geography
• Have a strong interest in sustainability, regenerative systems, and the organization of global supply chains
• Strong speaking and writing skills in English
Further, the following qualities will be valued highly in the assessment:

• Research vision and potential 
• Evidence of academic accomplishment (e.g., high grades, timely graduation)
• Knowledge and experience with qualitative research methods and empirical fieldwork 
• Scholarly/academic writing skills 
• Familiarity with Kenya’s socio-cultural context, or experience in settings with transferable relevance, is desirable but not required.
Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. The allowance will be agreed upon with the relevant union. The period of employment is 3 years. The envisaged starting date is as soon as possible. The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Lara Schilling (larasc@dtu.dk) and Lærke Højgaard Christiansen (laerc@dtu.dk)

You can read more about the Department of Technology, Management and Economics at https://www.man.dtu.dk/english

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 15 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time).

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A research statement (2–3 pages) outlining your research ideas and explaining your suitability for carrying out the project. Please engage with relevant scholarly literature on regenerative supply chains and organization. The statement is intended to demonstrate your research interests and potential; it is not a binding proposal, and the research plan may be further developed and refined in collaboration with the supervisory team upon enrolment in the PhD program.
• One copy of a selected written work (e.g., master’s thesis)
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

About DTU Management
DTU Management conducts excellent research at the intersection of management, technology and economics. We develop solutions in close cooperation with companies and public authorities. Our research aims at strengthening welfare, productivity and sustainability. A key element is the role of technology and its interaction with industry and individuals. The department offers a wide range of courses and programs at bachelor, master, and PhD levels across DTU's study programs. The department has 250+ employees with around half of staff coming from abroad. 

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

We are looking for a highly motivated and dynamic postdoc for a 2 year position to commence 1/1-2027.

  The position concerns pharmacological studies of an important regulator of synaptic plasticity in the mammalian brain.

  Information about the research group and work place can be found at the lab (Wellendorph lab) and department (www.drug.ku.dk) websites.

  Our research
 Our lab is devoted to understanding brain mechanisms involving the inhibitory neurotransmitter GABA (γ-aminobutyric acid) and its metabolite GHB (γ-hydroxybutyric acid) via their actions on their respective targets, including CaM-responsive kinase CaMKIIa. We use biochemical and pharmacological analyses in cells, tissues and whole organisms to elucidate the role of GHB and GABA targets in brain dysfunction. 

  The lab spans over many different techniques and backgrounds, making it a highly interdisciplinary work environment. In the group we value social interaction, openness and teamwork, with room for ambition and scientific excitement.

  Your job
 This specific postdoc project seeks to characterize the neuropharmacology of the target CaMKIIa using in-house generated compounds. This entails studies in vivo in mice as well as tissue- and cell-based biochemical and pharmacological analyses. We are looking for a postdoc with a strong basis in neuropharmacology particularly in vivo studies in mice and who can combine biochemistry, neuroscience and pharmacology. Your tasks will include planning and execution of in vivo experiments, primary neuron experiments and biochemical and pharmacological assays. This entails a curiosity for science and a systematic approach to doing research and exploring new ideas. In addition to doing research, it is expected that you supervise students and engage in departmental teaching according to norms (currently 100 hours of total teaching per year).

jobs.occupation: Legal Counsel
jobs.description:
Are you ready to take on the challenge of strengthening Orifarm's contract management capabilities and providing first-class, pragmatic legal advice across our international organization? Then we would love to hear from you

About the job

In this role, you will act as a trusted legal business partner across the organisation translating legal risks into practical, business-oriented solutions. We are looking for an ambitious and commercially minded legal professional who is motivated by working closely with the business and taking ownership of a broad range of commercial contracts_.

You will work closely with key stakeholders in Procurement, Business Development, CMO, Commercial and other business functions, contributing to a broad range of legal matters across the Group_.

You will:

• Draft, review and negotiate a wide range of commercial agreements, and advise on contract interpretation, amendments, breaches, terminations and contract-related disputes

• Drive and further develop Orifarm's Contract Lifecycle Management framework, including drafting, maintaining and improving contract templates, playbooks and standard clauses

• Develop and implement contract management policies, processes and governance structures

• Explore and drive the opportunities offered by AI and other legal technologies within contract management and legal processes

• Administer and optimise the company's contract management system

• Participate in M&A projects, including legal due diligence, and post-merger integration support

• Support strategic and operational decision-making across the organisation and provide general legal support in areas such as marketing law, intellectual property, corporate law, commercial law and general business law matters together with the rest of the legal team

You will be part of Group Legal and report directly to Orifarm's General Counsel, Lars Brøgger.

Who are you?

You hold a degree in law (LL.M.) or hold a degree in business law (e.g. cand.merc.jur.). You have a minimum of three years of relevant professional experience, including solid experience drafting_,_ reviewing and negotiating commercial contracts, gained in an international company or law firm. You bring an interest in or hands-on experience with Contract Lifecycle Management and the digitalisation of legal processes_.

You are energised by working closely with colleagues across the business and thrive in a collaborative, team-oriented environment. You embrace change and enjoy taking the lead in complex negotiations. You work independently and in a structured manner and build strong relationships internally and externally.

Who are we?

By joining Group Legal, you will become part of a dedicated legal team in an international and ambitious company. In addition to the General Counsel, the team currently consists of two lawyers, Helene Arensbak Mørk and Rasmus Sell Ditlevsen, and we collaborate closely with two lawyers based in Germany, in our Legal Affairs, Pharma Trade team. We offer a dynamic and informal working environment focused on collaboration_,_ quality and continuous improvement_.

Why should you join Orifarm?

jobs.occupation: Assistant professor or Assistant professor Tenure Track, Department of Computer Science, Copenhagen Section
jobs.description:
Assistant professor or Assistant professor Tenure Track, Department of Computer Science, Copenhagen Section

Department of Computer Science, Aalborg University is hiring Assistant professors or Assistant professors Tenure Track starting February 1, 2027. The Assistant professor position is a 3-year fixed term full-time position, and the tenure track position, is a structured career pathway with clearly defined criteria for progression to a permanent position upon successful evaluation.

One position will be affiliated with the research group Probabilistic and Symbolic AI in the Copenhagen section.

One position will be affiliated with the research group Data Engineering, Science, and Systems in the Copenhagen section.

About the CPH Section

The CPH Section is organised around the Software education programme at AAU’s Copenhagen campus and spans a broad range of computer science research. The two positions in this call will strengthen the section’s profiles in Probabilistic and Symbolic AI (PSAI), covering probabilistic, symbolic and neuro-symbolic approaches to AI, and Data Engineering, Science, and Systems (DESS), focusing on methods and systems for managing and analysing complex data. The section also hosts research in areas including natural language processing and trustworthy AI, human-centred computing, software engineering, and distributed and interactive systems. This breadth supports collaboration across research groups and between foundational, methodological and application-oriented research.

The CPH Section is a growing and international academic environment with an informal and collegial working culture. We aim to combine high scientific ambition with openness, mutual respect and a sustainable working life. Staff have substantial academic freedom and responsibility and are encouraged to collaborate across research groups and career stages, contribute to shared research and teaching activities, and develop an independent academic profile. As a member of the section, you will be part of both a close local community in Copenhagen and broader departmental research groups and network.

Qualification requirements

Appointment as assistant professor requires academic qualifications at PhD level. The research potential of each applicant will be emphasized in the overall assessment.

Your work tasks

We offer an attractive career opportunity for promising and talented researchers from around the world. The position is a career development position with the possibility of transitioning to a tenured associate professorship. We will work together with you to develop your research talent through supervision, professional networks and pedagogical upgrading.

As tenure track assistant professor your primary tasks will be research and research-based teaching. You will teach and supervise students at bachelor’s and master’s level, and you will contribute to the development of the department through research of international quality. In your daily work, you will work closely with both Danish and international colleagues.

Your main tasks will consist of:

• Independent research of the highest international quality including publication.

• Teaching, guidance and examination of bachelor’s and master’s degree students, as well as possible supervision of PhD students.

• Some degree of contribution towards attracting external research funding.

• The opportunity to collaborate with relevant national and international research environments.

You will report to the Head of Department Peter Axel Nielsen.

Your competencies

We are looking for applicants with independent research-related qualifications at a high international level and a PhD degree in computer science or a related field, and you show potential to become one of the best in the academic field of the position. You are a clear communicator with potential of becoming a skilled group leader, and you can, under guidance, organize and conduct supervision and teaching at bachelor’s and master’s degree level. Completed pedagogical courses in supervision or similar will be a plus, as will experience with external research collaborations. We also draw attention to a stay or employment at one or more internationally recognised research institutions.

As a person, you have good interpersonal skills, are inclusive and team-oriented and able to contribute to a good work environment.

We expect you to be able to write and speak English at the academic level.

Tenure track positions are usually aimed at candidates who have not previously held an assistant professor position. In order to be assessed qualified for a tenure track assistant professor position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Department of Computer Science

Department of Computer Science at Aalborg University is highly regarded among researchers, students, and external partners because of our leading research, education, and collaboration. The department currently has more than 165 scientific staff, 20 administrative staff, and 1100 students.

Our research is recognized internationally and nationally to be at the highest level of excellence according to community standards, prioritizing quality over quantity. We balance applications and theory, and societal and scientific impact, applying research to solve real-world problems, while also conducing foundational research with potential long-term impact. As part of this, we are acknowledged and respected for close collaboration with industry and for applying research to create impact and value for society.

Our educations are problem-based and recognized for producing highly skilled graduates with very high employability, who are experienced with project work on solving real-world problems in diverse teams and able to think critically about the technologies they develop.

You can read more on www.cs.aau.dk, and you can read more about the TECH faculty here.

Denmark builds on a welfare system, and while taxes are high, there are plenty of welfare services including free education and healthcare including pay during paternity/maternity leave and during sickness. Find more information at the International Staff Unit – they also offer a spouse/partner programme.

Assessment in connection with transfer to associate professorship

The assessment in connection with transition to tenure as an associate professor normally takes place in the final six months of the tenure track assistant professors’ employment. However, the employee may request that an assessment take place at an earlier time in the first four years. If this assessment finds that the employee is not academically qualified, they may request another assessment within the final six months of their period of employment. A maximum of two assessments may take place.

In order to be qualified for an associate professor position, you must meet these academic criteria.

Appointed candidates will have to make a tenure track career plan with the head of department/immediate superior to align expectations and indicate the objectives for the tenure track’s development process. This career plan must be satisfactory followed and accomplished for the tenure track assistant professor to be assessed qualified.

Additionally, the assessment, on transition to the associate professorship, will as a minimum, emphasize the following qualifications in relation to the scientific subject area of the tenure track assistant professorship:

Research qualifications equivalent to the level that can be achieved on the basis of satisfactorily completed employment as tenure track assistant professor.

Documented scientific production at international level. Assessment will be based on up to ten selected publications selected by the employee.

Documentation of pedagogical supervision and upgrading of qualifications, including a positive written assessment of teaching qualifications. The assessment will also be based on the employee's teaching portfolio. The level of contribution to an active academic environment as well as the ability to collaborate and build relationships.

The level of experience with grant proposals and experience of communicating research to relevant stakeholders.

Appointed candidates will have to make a tenure track career plan with the head of department/immediate superior, to align expectations and indicate the objectives for the tenure track’s development process. This career plan must be satisfactory followed and accomplished in order for the tenure track assistant professor to be assessed qualified.

If the tenure track assistant professor fails to request that their qualifications be assessed in the last year of their period of employment or if they are assessed as not academically qualified, the university must immediately initiate dismissal proceedings in accordance with the collective agreement rules.

How to apply

Your application must include the following:

• Application, stating reasons for applying, qualifications in relation to the position, and intentions and visions for the position

• Curriculum Vitae (CV)

• Diplomas (master's degree diploma and PhD diploma)

• List of publications, with an indication of the attached publications that you wish to be taken into account in the assessment. You may attach a maximum of five publications.

• Documentation of teaching qualifications. Please see guidelines for teaching portfolio at The Technical Faculty of IT and Design.

• Dissemination qualifications, including participation on committees or boards, participation in organisations etc.

• Additional qualifications in relation to the position

• References/recommendations

You can read more about the requirements for your application here.

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website.

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Aalborg University has a policy of parallel language use. International staff are encouraged, with support from the university, to learn Danish during their employment in order to support their integration into the workplace and Danish society.

Danish language courses will be offered as part of the employment.

Do you have any questions? If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information

Read more about our recruitment process here

The appointment process at Aalborg University involves a shortlisting process. You can read more about the shortlisting and appointment process here.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Salary and terms of employment  The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement) and protocol on certain terms of employment of academic staff at universities.

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “Assistant professor”.

There is a mutual probationary period of 3 months for the position.

Aalborg University - Knowledge for the world

Aalborg University is an international workplace with more than 3,700 employees. We offer real-world-oriented education and create world-class research results through collaboration between researchers, students, and public and private companies. This is how we achieve insights, new solutions to societal problems, and knowledge that changes the world. Our main campus is in Aalborg, but we also have campuses in Esbjerg and Copenhagen.

Contacts

• Professor Johannes Bjerva: jbjerva@cs.aau.dk

jobs.description:
PhD position in Reversible Programming Languages (MSCA Doctoral Network E-CoRe, DC1), University of Copenhagen
 
 The position is doctoral candidate DC1, “Reversible Programming Languages", in the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network E-CoRe. The position is available from 1 January 2027, or after agreement.
 
 Job description
 The Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section, part of the Department of Computer Science (DIKU), University of Copenhagen, invites applications for a 3-year PhD position on reversible programming languages.
 
 The project
 The position is funded by the European Union under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks (MSCA-DN) programme, grant agreement no. 101120187. The project advances the science and practice of reversible computing for a sustainable digital future. Energy is a main concern in society: IT accounts for an estimated 10% of global energy consumption. Reversible computation discards no information and therefore avoids the fundamental energy lower bound of conventional computing. The network trains a cohort of doctoral candidates who will improve and popularize reversible languages, algorithms, and architectures for energy-intensive applications.
 
 Read more about the network at https://e-core.nws.cs.unibo.it/.

  The position is open for talented candidates with a master’s degree, who want to pursue a PhD degree in Computer Science.

  DC1: The successful PhD candidate will work on reversible programming languages. The candidate can build on the work by project members.
 
 Concretely, the work includes the following:

   	
• Advancing reversible programming languages with a view on increasing their expressiveness and applicability to the development and construction of non-trivial reversible algorithms. 	
• Studying the integration of reversible features into mainstream irreversible languages. 	
• Exploring domain-specific features to identify novel language idioms specific to reversible programming and applications developed elsewhere in the network. 	
• Publishing the results at international conferences and in peer-reviewed journals.   Planned secondments: CNRS / Université Côte d'Azur (France), University of Southern Denmark (Denmark), and Tokai National Higher Education and Research System (Japan).

  Key criteria for the assessment of applicants for the position:
 The candidate must have a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish Master's degree) in Computer Science or a closely related field, obtained by the recruitment date.

  Certified copy of original Master of Science diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in a language other than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted.

  As a prerequisite for a PhD fellowship employment, your master’s degree must be equivalent to a Danish master’s degree. We encourage you to read more in the assessment database: https://ufsn.dk/english/education/recognition-and-transparency/find-assessments/assessment-database/ 

  Please note that we might ask you to obtain an assessment of your education performed by the Ministry of Higher Education and Science.

  Other important criteria are:

   	
• Strong academic record and motivation for doctoral research.  	
• Experience in programming language design, semantics, or implementation, regardless of programming paradigm, is an advantage. Prior knowledge of reversible computing is not needed. 	
• Ability to work independently, take initiative, and collaborate effectively in an international research environment. Proactive and team-oriented approach to work. 	
• Proficiency in written and spoken English. 	
• Willingness and ability to travel and undertake secondments at other project partners.   The successful candidate will be employed as a PhD student at the Department of Computer Science at the Faculty of Sciences, University of Copenhagen, and will collaborate closely with the group at the University of Southern Denmark, Odense, which is also an E-CoRe partner. The position may involve co-supervising related student projects. The PhD student is expected to participate in the activities of the research section and in the training programme of the E-CoRe network.
 
 The main supervisor is Professor Robert Glück (e-mail: glueck@di.ku.dk), whose current research focus is on programming languages, reversible computing, program generation, and metaprogramming.

  Start date:    1 January 2027, or after agreement with the cohort of the MSCA-DN

  Duration:      3 years

  The successful candidate will conduct independent research related to the topics above at the Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section, Department of Computer Science (DIKU). We expect the candidate to engage in an active research environment and take part in student guidance.

  Note: Another job opening for DC7 “Compilation Principles for Reversible Languages” is available. More information: XXX-LINK-TO-DC7.

  Mobility rule
 The researcher must not have resided or carried out his/her/their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Denmark for more than 12 months in the 3 years immediately before the recruitment date. Short stays as holidays and compulsory military service and/or Refugee Convention 1951 are disregarded.

  Eligibility as Doctoral Candidate (DC)
 The recruited DC must be doctoral candidate, i.e. not already in possession of a doctoral degree on the first day of employment. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree will not be considered eligible.
 
 Workplace description 
 The Programming Languages and Theory of Computation (PLTC) Section is part of the Department of Computer Science (DIKU) at the Faculty of Science, located on the North Campus in Copenhagen. At the section we research topics such as algorithmic aspects of programming, compiler technology, functional programming, reversible and quantum computing. You will be part of an international group of PhD students, postdocs, and faculty working at the intersection of programming languages, theory of computing, and various applications.

  More information about PLTC and DIKU can be found at https://di.ku.dk/english/research/pltc/  and https://di.ku.dk/english/.

  Terms of employment 
 Salary, pension and terms of employment will be in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant organization. Currently, the monthly salary starts at DKK 31,845 / approx. EUR 4,260 (August 2026-level). 
 Depending on qualifications, a supplement may be negotiated. The employer will pay an additional 18.07 % to your pension fund.
 
 The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025.

  Further information
 For further information, please contact Professor Robert Glück (e-mail: glueck@di.ku.dk).

  International applicants may find this link useful: https://ism.ku.dk/ (International Staff Mobility) or https://www.workindenmark.dk/.

  Application procedure
 Your online application must be submitted in English by clicking ‘Apply now’ below. Furthermore, your application must include the following documents/attachments – all in PDF format:

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page). 	
• CV incl. education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position. 	
• Master of Science diploma and transcript of records. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor will do. 	
• Publication list (if any).   Deadline for applications: Sunday 1 November 2026, 23:59 PM CET.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the above-mentioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the hiring committee which will consist of both internal (UCPH) and external members. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment by an unbiased assessor. Once the assessment work has been completed, each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself.

  You may read about the recruitment process at https://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.
 
 The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

jobs.occupation: Postdoc in the Strep A Vaccine Research Group at the NIVI Research Center, Department of Immunology and Microbiology
jobs.description:
We are looking for a highly motivated and curious postdoctoral fellow who has experience in protein biochemistry, enzymology, recombinant protein expression, and functional assay development.

  The position is initially available for 24 months. An extension may be possible subject to project progress, funding and mutual agreement. The position is expected to commence on 1 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter, as agreed with the successful candidate.

  The fellow will join the Strep A Vaccine Research Group led by A/Prof Stephan Brouwer at the Novo Nordisk Foundation Initiative for Vaccines and Immunity (NIVI) Research Center, which is embedded in the Department of Immunology and Microbiology, Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences, University of Copenhagen.

  Background

  The Novo Nordisk Foundation Initiative for Vaccines and Immunity (NIVI), launched in December 2023, has a unique mission to harness airway immunity through innovative vaccine research and development to prevent airborne epidemics. NIVI has two parts:

   	
• NIVI Research Center (NIVI-R): A state-of-the-art research center anchored to the University of Copenhagen, Department of Immunology and Microbiology. 	
• NIVI Development (NIVI-D): A company that focuses on translational sciences and advancing vaccine development.   NIVI-R conducts scientific research, while NIVI-D works to quickly turn that research into new vaccine candidates. NIVI-D accelerates clinical trials (phases 1 and 2) and ensures a smooth transition to partners for later stages of development.

  By connecting science, innovation, clinical trials, regulatory processes, and product development, NIVI aims to streamline the journey from research to real-world vaccines.

  Our research

  Our group is part of the NIVI-R interdisciplinary research consortium and focuses on the discovery, characterization, and evaluation of vaccine antigens from Streptococcus pyogenes (Group A Streptococcus; Strep A). Strep A is responsible for a substantial global burden of disease, ranging from pharyngitis and skin infections to life-threatening invasive disease and post-infectious autoimmune complications. Despite decades of research, no licensed vaccine is currently available.

  Our research aims to better understand the molecular mechanisms underlying Strep A pathogenesis and protective immunity, and to translate this knowledge into the development of next-generation vaccines. We combine bacterial genetics, molecular microbiology, biochemistry, protein science, functional immunology, human cellular models, and pre-clinical infection models to identify and evaluate vaccine antigens and immune correlates of protection.

  A major focus of the group is the development of functional assays to characterize Strep A virulence factors and vaccine antigens. These assays are used to define biological function, investigate host-pathogen interactions, evaluate antibody-mediated neutralization, and establish mechanistic links between antigen-specific immune responses and protection.

  We are a young, international, and collaborative team that values scientific rigor, creativity, mentorship, and teamwork. As part of NIVI, we work closely with leading groups in airway immunity, vaccine formulation and adjuvants, structural biology, and we benefit from close ties to Statens Serum Institut and to NIVI-D’s translational pipeline. We are committed to fostering an inclusive and supportive research environment and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds; we value diversity across gender, nationality, career stage, and scientific training.

  Your job

  We strive to build a cohesive research environment in which individual projects contribute to a shared goal: developing and validating vaccine antigens that can advance Strep A vaccine development. As our new postdoctoral fellow, you will lead the development and implementation of functional assays for the characterization of Strep A antigens and virulence factors.

  Your primary responsibilities will include designing, developing, optimizing, and validating biochemical, enzymatic, cellular, and immunological assays to investigate antigen function and assess vaccine-induced antibody responses. You will contribute to recombinant protein production and characterization, establish functional readouts for antigen activity, and develop assays suitable for evaluating antibody-mediated inhibition or neutralization of virulence-associated mechanisms.

  The project will involve extensive laboratory work encompassing molecular cloning, recombinant protein expression, protein purification, protein characterization, enzymology, and cell-based assays. In addition, you will contribute to the development of opsonophagocytic killing (OPK) assays and other functional immune assays using relevant human cell culture systems.

  You will be expected to independently drive your research project with a high degree of scientific autonomy while actively collaborating with colleagues within the group and the broader NIVI consortium. Responsibilities will also include data analysis, manuscript preparation, presentation of results at group and consortium meetings, and dissemination of findings at international conferences. The successful candidate will benefit from regular mentoring and career-development discussions tailored to their professional goals.

  The project will include the following key areas:

   	
• Development and validation of biochemical and enzymatic assays to characterize Strep A vaccine antigens and virulence-associated proteins. 	
• Recombinant expression, purification, and biophysical characterization of bacterial proteins required for functional assay development. 	
• Development of antibody-functional assays, including neutralization, inhibition, and mechanism-of-action studies. 	
• Establishment and optimization of opsonophagocytic killing (OPK) assays and other cellular assays relevant to vaccine-induced protection. 	
• Investigation of host-pathogen interactions using mammalian cell culture systems and functional immunological assays.   While the precise experimental emphasis may evolve as the project progresses, the successful candidate is expected to contribute across these interconnected areas, with a primary focus on establishing robust functional assays that support antigen discovery, characterization, and vaccine evaluation.

  Profile

  We are looking for a highly motivated and creative scientist with the following competencies and experience:

  Essential experience and skills

   	
• You have a PhD in Biochemistry, Molecular Biology, Microbiology, Immunology, or a closely related field. 	
• You have significant hands-on experience developing, optimizing, and troubleshooting biochemical, enzymatic, or protein-based functional assays. 	
• You have strong expertise in recombinant protein expression, purification, and characterization. 	
• You possess a solid understanding of protein biochemistry, enzyme kinetics, protein-protein interactions, and structure-function relationships. 	
• You have experience with molecular cloning and standard molecular biology techniques. 	
• You have experience working with mammalian cell culture systems. 	
• You have demonstrated ability to independently design experiments and solve complex technical challenges. 	
• You have a strong record of scientific productivity, as demonstrated by peer-reviewed publications and other scientific achievements. 	
• You are collaborative, communicative, and enjoy working in an interdisciplinary team environment. 	
• You have excellent English communication skills, both written and spoken. 	
• You are motivated to develop new methods and expand your scientific expertise.   Desirable experience and skills

   	
• Experience with bacterial pathogens and host-pathogen interaction research. 	
• Experience developing antibody-functional assays, including neutralization, inhibition, or immune-effector assays. 	
• Experience with opsonophagocytic killing (OPK) assays or related phagocyte-based functional assays. 	
• Experience with primary immune cells, macrophage cell lines, neutrophil-like cell lines, or other relevant cellular models. 	
• Experience with biophysical protein characterization techniques, such as SPR, SEC-MALS, CD spectroscopy, or related methods. 	
• Experience with protein structural analysis or structure-guided antigen characterization.   Overall, it is expected that you contribute actively to a positive, collaborative and productive work environment. A strong scientific track record with a productive publication list will also weigh strongly in the assessment.

DAWN brings together experts in all aspects of early Universe research and is deeply involved in major existing and upcoming surveys with JWST and HST (e.g. SPURS, COSMOS3D, FRESCO, COSMOS-Web, RUBIES, BEACON, and CLUTCH), ALMA (e.g. CHAMPS), and Euclid (e.g. Cosmic Dawn Survey of the deep fields), as well as simulations.

  DAWN Postdoctoral Fellowships are intended for outstanding scientists whose research falls within DAWN’s research themes focused on the early Universe: first stars, high-redshift galaxy evolution, reionization and evolution of the IGM, high-redshift transients and supernovae, dust and ISM in the early Universe, massive galaxy evolution, and dark matter. jobs.occupation: PhD scholarships in Economics at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark
jobs.description:
Applications are invited for one fully funded PhD scholarship at the Department of Economics, University of Southern Denmark. The position is based at SDU’s Esbjerg campus.

The successful candidate will be enrolled in the 5+3 PhD programme. The programme includes a research stay abroad, typically of six months’ duration, and offers a competitive full-time salary.

We aim to appoint the successful candidate as soon as possible, ideally with a start date of 15 January 2027, while remaining flexible regarding the exact timing.

About the Department and Research Environment

The Department of Economics is an international department with a strong tradition of excellence in research and teaching across a wide range of fields within economics. Research, teaching, and outreach activities are organized within five research groups: Econometrics and Data Science; Economic History; Macroeconomics; Microeconomics; and Environmental and Resource Economics. Further information about the department and its research groups is available on the department website.

The PhD student will be affiliated with the Environmental and Resource Economics (ERE) group, which focuses on Environmental and Natural resource economics on a variety of topics, namely ecosystem conservation and use, marine resource use, management and conservation, energy transitions, climate regulation, and interdisciplinary research at the interface between economics and the natural sciences. The group applies economic theory and tools to policy and analysis to provide guidance for more efficient use of environmental and natural resource goods and services.

The position

The successful candidate will become part of an international research environment and work closely with Associate Professors Ana Faria Lopes and Melina Kourantidou.  Part of the work will contribute to the BRAVE (Biological Invasions Resolved through Adaptable, Versatile, and Engaging Nature-Based Solutions) project, a Biodiversa+ -funded project that investigates the complex ecological and societal challenges associated with invasive species and their management. In particular, the research will contribute to the Danish BRAVE case study on the invasive Pacific oyster in the Wadden Sea, including work on stakeholder preferences, economic values, and trade-offs associated with its management. For further information about the project, please see this link or this link.

The project relies on the application of economic theories, namely non-market valuation and bioeconomic modelling, to investigate the management of invasive species. We welcome candidates with strong quantitative and analytical skills from economics or related disciplines, including candidates with interdisciplinary backgrounds and an interest in environmental and resource management.  There will be considerable scope for the PhD student to develop their own research questions within the broader themes of the project.

The successful candidate is expected to contribute to high-quality research within the scope of the project, through both collaborative research and independent work, including a single-authored paper. In addition, the candidate will be involved in teaching and supervision within economics at both undergraduate and graduate levels.

The PhD student will be supervised by Associate Professor Ana Faria Lopes as the main supervisor and will join a research group that includes postdoctoral researcher and research assistants, with access to an international network of collaborators.

Applicants’ profile

Applicants should have completed a relevant master’s degree in Environmental and Resource Management, Economics, Mathematics and Economics, or related disciplines. Furthermore, we expect applicants to:

• 
Have solid quantitative and analytical skills, with experience in data analysis and applied quantitative methods using R, Stata, or similar tools, and be eager to learn and apply new methods.

• 
Be dedicated, capable of working independently and collaboratively as part of a research team.

• 
Have strong English skills, both spoken and written. 

• 
Have willingness to participate in stakeholder engagement activities and communicate research findings to different audiences. 

• 
Have good interpersonal skills, be interested in engaging with national and international researchers.

The following qualifications are an advantage

• 
Have an interest in, or potentially experience with, non-market valuation, press analysis, GIS and/or bioeconomic modelling.

• 
Experience conducting empirical research.

• 
Demonstrated interest in environmental and resource economics.

• 
Knowledge of Danish or another Scandinavian language would be an advantage for stakeholder engagement and work with locally relevant material but is not a requirement.

We are an international department, and the working language is English.

Further information about the position can be obtained from Head of Administration Astrid Holm Nielsen, e-mail: astni@sam.sdu.dk. For general questions regarding relocation, housing, taxes etc., contact the SDU’s International Staff Office. 

How to apply for this position

Employment as a paid PhD fellow takes place in accordance with the circular of 20 December 2021 on the collective agreement for academics in the state – appendix 5, protocol on PhD fellowships.

For more information on the department guidelines for qualification and recruitment please see our Appointment Guidelines.

The application must include (all attachments must be in Adobe PDF format): 

• 
Detailed CV - the education and work history must be month and year specific.

• 
A certified copy of your master’s degree certificate, including transcripts of all examination results.  Foreign diplomas that are not in Norwegian, Swedish or English must be accompanied by a translation into Danish or English, as well as a translation of the official description of the marking scale used.

• 
A motivational letter describing why the applicant is a good match for analyzing the topic and how the applicant’s skills provide a solid foundation to do so (max. 5 pages incl. reference list).

• 
A project description (max 5 pages of 2400 characters each, including spaces, notes, appendices, bibliography etc.).

• 
When applying for a PhD scholarship, please fill in the application form available on our web page. 

On the webpage of the PhD-school, you can find the guidelines for preparing your project proposal.

All non-Danish documents must be translated into English.

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material.

Once the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicant will receive the portion of the evaluation that pertains to them.

Applications that are incomplete regarding the above requirements will not be assessed by the committee.

Shortlisting and tests may be used in the assessment process.

As part of the overall assessment of the applicant’s qualifications, an interview may be applied.

Documents should not contain a CPR number (civil registration number) – in this case, the CPR number must be crossed out.

The application and CV must not exceed 10 MB.

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, 23.59 CET/CEST.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now" on our website. Uploaded files must be in Adobe PDF (unlocked) or Word format.

We recommend that you read the guideline for applicants. If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk before the application deadline.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position.

Salary and employment terms

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements.

As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process.

SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary.
